item.title: James Lee Jerkins
item.description: James Lee Jerkins, 61, of Summerdale, died Jan. 25, 2026. Born in Brewton, he is remembered by family and friends; celebration of life Feb. 21 at New Vision Church.

item.title: Dr. Sara Faison Lawhorne
item.description: Educator and business leader Dr. Sara Faison Lawhorne whose career spanned classrooms, family entertainment centers and corporate leadership, died Jan. 13, 2026, after a battle with pancreatic cancer.

item.title: James Edward Jackson
item.description: James Edward Jackson, 80, devoted deacon and top JC Penney furniture salesman, remembered by four daughters after his January 13, 2026 passing.

item.title: Gladys Jones Culliver
item.description: Remembering Gladys Jones Culliver (1946–2026), a devoted mother, grandmother, and longtime housekeeper, whose faith and service shaped her family and church.

item.title: REGISTRATION IS OPEN FOR SPRING SPORTS
item.description: REGISTRATION IS OPEN FOR SPRING SPORTS

item.title: Chipped EBT cards heading to users
item.description: Alabama EBT cardholders are getting new chip-enabled cards that require activation and default to blocking out-of-state and online purchases for added benefit protection.

item.title: County leaders stall tax levy
item.description: Escambia County delays hospital tax levy vote amid questions over healthcare authority plans and transparency, set to reconvene Wednesday.

item.title: Brewton Police steps up patrol on South Boulevard
item.description: After recent fatal crashes, Brewton police are increasing patrols on South Boulevard, meaning drivers will see more enforcement during morning and afternoon traffic.

item.title: E-edition for February 11, 2026
item.description: Explore the February 11, 2026 e-edition of The Brewton Standard for the latest news and updates from around the community.

item.title: Hospital tax levy approved by Commissioners
item.description: Escambia County commissioners approve a 4-mill hospital tax levy for 2026 in a 4-1 vote, following voter authorization in 2025, and secure a $1.3M grant for Chavers Creek Bridge work.
